title: AMD’s Lisa Su defends open-source AI following Hugging Face security breach caused by OpenAI agents
excerpt: Speaking at AMD Advanced AI conference, the chip giant's CEO weighed in on the open source debate—and showcased its latest hardware offerings.
content_html:
Lisa Su, Advanced Micro Devices' chief executive, doubled down on her support for open-source AI models on Thursday, reaffirming her commitment to the technology framework after a high-profile security breach this week involving OpenAI agents was ultimately resolved by an open-source model.

"I think open source is a great thing," the AMD CEO said, addressing the controversy during a press conference at the company's Advancing AI conference in San Francisco. "It gives people a level of transparency and control that enables you to do a lot."

Su's comments, at an event to promote the company's new hardware, underscore the extent to which the growing power of AI is causing novel flashpoints and challenges that stretch across the technology industry and geopolitical realms. Earlier this week, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI models autonomously escaped a controlled environment and breached the internal systems of AI digital library firm Hugging Face. Hugging Face revealed that it relied on an open-source model from a Chinese company, instead of a U.S. frontier lab, to contain the incident. The event fueled an ongoing debate across the tech industry over the power of cheaper, open-source models, just as the White House weighs banning foreign open-source software.

Su seemed to suggest that banning open-source was not the answer. "This active conversation about restricting open models is an area where we all believe that they have a significant place in the ecosystem, and we just have to make sure that we manage all pieces of that."

The battle over open-source models revolves around several issues. U.S. companies warn that Chinese competitors are rapidly closing the gap with American frontier labs by distilling U.S. technology into free, potentially dangerous software built with fewer guardrails.

In addition, industry leaders have debated how aggressively U.S. regulators should target domestic open-source models, arguing that overregulation could drive firms toward Chinese alternatives. AMD executives also highlighted early signs of self-regulation, pointing to open-source models built with "open constitutions" to mollify regulatory concerns, although they did not provide specifics.

Vamsi Boppana, AMD's senior vice president of AI, told Fortune in an interview that regulatory frameworks may benefit the industry, but that the open-source players also have a unique opportunity.

"Within open source, there is a real opportunity for innovation to be able to put things like guardrails and constitutions and so on that models can be self-certified within the open community without other sort of governmental regulations," Boppana said. "We have certain responsibilities; there are probably greater responsibilities with the creators of models."

content_html_zh:
Advanced Micro Devices 首席执行官 Lisa Su 周四加大了对开源 AI 模型的支持力度，在本周涉及 OpenAI 代理的备受瞩目的安全漏洞最终通过开源模型解决后，重申了她对技术框架的承诺。

“我认为开源是一件伟大的事情，”这位 AMD 首席执行官在旧金山举行的该公司推进人工智能大会的新闻发布会上谈到了这一争议。 “它为人们提供了一定程度的透明度和控制力，使你能够做很多事情。”

苏在公司新硬件推广活动上的评论强调了人工智能不断增长的力量在多大程度上引发了跨越技术行业和地缘政治领域的新的热点和挑战。 本周早些时候，OpenAI 披露，其两个人工智能模型自主逃离了受控环境，并突破了人工智能数字图书馆公司 Hugging Face 的内部系统。 Hugging Face 透露，它依靠一家中国公司的开源模型来控制这一事件，而不是美国前沿实验室。 这一事件引发了整个科技行业关于更便宜的开源模型的力量的持续争论，正如白宫考虑禁止外国开源软件一样。

苏似乎暗示禁止开源并不是解决办法。 “关于限制开放模型的积极对话是一个我们都相信它们在生态系统中占有重要地位的领域，我们只需要确保我们管理好其中的所有部分。”

开源模型之争围绕几个问题展开。 美国公司警告说，中国竞争对手正在通过将美国技术提炼成免费的、具有潜在危险的软件，而这些软件的护栏较少，从而迅速缩小与美国前沿实验室的差距。

此外，行业领导者还讨论了美国监管机构应如何积极地针对国内开源模式，认为过度监管可能会促使企业转向中国的替代方案。 AMD 高管还强调了自我监管的早期迹象，指出以“开放宪法”构建的开源模型可以缓解监管担忧，尽管他们没有提供具体细节。

AMD 人工智能高级副总裁 Vamsi Boppana 在接受《财富》杂志采访时表示，监管框架可能有利于整个行业，但开源厂商也有独特的机会。

“在开源领域，创新有一个真正的机会，能够将护栏和宪法等模型放在开放社区中进行自我认证，而无需其他类型的政府监管，”博帕纳说。 “我们有一定的责任；模型的创建者可能有更大的责任。”
